abstract: The sharp rise in long-term interest rates since 2020 is difficult to explain from slow-moving fundamentals. This column shows that narrow windows around nonfarm payroll releases and speeches by prominent Federal Reserve policymakers capture 80-90% of the observed increase in long-term US yields, despite covering only 24% of trading days. These events primarily shift expectations about the policy-rate path rather than the natural rate of interest. This suggests that natural rate of interest may anchor long-term rates less firmly than standard theory assumes, allowing shifts in monetary policy perceptions to generate persistent, and potentially self-validating, movements in yields.
authors: Paul Beaudry, Paolo Cavallino, Tim Willems
title: Anatomy of a rise: Monetary policy and the post-Covid surge in long-term interest rates
title_zh: 上升的剖析：货币政策与后疫情时代长期利率的飙升

abstract: Although much of the persistence literature has dealt with extractive colonial institutions, no study directly examines the persistent effects of the transition from pure subsistence to market economies as a result of such institutions. This article fills that gap by investigating the paddy commutation system of British Ceylon, which taxed native farmers in cash on the potential yield of their paddy lands. On the basis of a novel dataset on nineteenth‐century Ceylon and a two‐pronged identification strategy of neighbouring unit analysis and propensity score matching, I find that historical exposure to the paddy commutation system predicts higher wealth today. Advanced agricultural markets, higher land ownership, and an ethos of economic independence resulting from the commutation system appear to be the primary mechanisms driving these more favourable wealth outcomes.
title: Blessing in disguise: The persistent economic legacy of the grain tax of British Ceylon
title_zh: 塞翁失马：英属锡兰谷物税的持久经济遗产

abstract: Our paper presents a causal machine learning (ML) methodology to study the heterogeneous effects of economy‐wide shocks and applies it to the impact of the COVID‐19 crisis on exports. This method is applicable in scenarios where, due to the pervasive nature of the shock, it is difficult to identify a control group that is not affected by the shock and to determine ex ante differences in shock intensity across units. In particular, our study investigates the effectiveness of different ML techniques in predicting firms' trade and, by building on recent developments in causal ML, these predictions are used to reconstruct the counterfactual distribution of firms' trade under different COVID‐19 scenarios and investigate the heterogeneity of treatment effects. Specifically, we focus on the probability of Colombian firms surviving in the export market under two different scenarios: a COVID‐19 setting and a non‐COVID‐19 counterfactual situation. On average, we find that the COVID‐19 shock decreased a firm's probability of surviving in the export market by about 20 percentage points in April 2020. We study the treatment effect heterogeneity by employing a classification analysis that compares the characteristics of the firms on the tails of the estimated distribution of the individual treatment effects.
journal: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics
title: Assessing the Heterogeneous Impact of Economy‐Wide Shocks: A Causal Machine Learning Approach Applied to Colombian Firms
title_zh: 评估经济整体冲击的异质性影响：一种应用于哥伦比亚企业的因果机器学习方法

abstract: We examine the effects of European integration on inward foreign direct investment (FDI) by disentangling the impacts of EU membership and euro adoption. Focusing on the 10 countries that joined the EU in 2004, we exploit the heterogeneous integration process in which seven countries subsequently adopted the euro while three retained independent currencies. Using the synthetic difference‐in‐differences estimator and Japanese firm‐level data, we find that EU membership increased the FDI probability by 3.64% for non‐EMU countries, while reducing it by 0.43% for EMU entrants. Euro adoption itself significantly lowered the FDI probability, a result also confirmed by complementary country‐level analysis. Consistent with our theoretical model, these effects are primarily driven by the manufacturing sector, where exchange rate flexibility serves as an operational hedge for export platforms. Overall, our findings highlight a fundamental trade‐off between market access and monetary integration.
title: Contrasting Effects of EU and EMU Membership on FDI: A Synthetic Difference‐in‐Differences Approach

abstract: Using an artefactual field experiment in a bilingual Swiss state with participants speaking different languages, this paper investigates how both heterogeneity and majority and minority statuses influence cooperation in a repeated multiple-level public good game in which participants can simultaneously contribute to a global good and local goods. Heterogeneity is based on language by using two native groups, German and French speakers, as our subject pool. We find that group heterogeneity has a negative effect on cooperation, which is mainly driven by a decrease in contributions to local public goods while contributions to the global good are not affected. The lower contributions to the local goods in the heterogeneous treatments are mainly due to lower contributions by majority members while the minority members contribute similar amounts to the reference group or even more. Furthermore, we observe that the impact of heterogeneity on contributions is magnified for individuals who are members of a linguistic minority in their real life. Finally, our article has implications for managerial and public policy, highlighting the fact that global heterogeneity can affect cooperation behaviors in local groups, even when they are homogeneous.
title: The Effects of Global and Local Heterogeneity on Cooperation in Multi-Level Public Goods: Experimental Evidence
title_zh: 全球与局部异质性对多层级公共物品合作的影响：实验证据

abstract: Which patents do firms allow to lapse, and who governs the decision? A U.S. patent remains in force only if its owner pays three scheduled maintenance fees. Many patents lapse; renewal records show which, but not how the choice is made. We hand-collect the IP-governance structures (board-level IP committees and dedicated IP officers) of all 7,735 patent-holding U.S. public firms over 1985–2019. Linking these to patent market values (Kogan et al. 2017) and USPTO maintenance-fee records, we measure how closely each firm’s lapse decisions align with the market’s valuation. We document five stylized facts. First, lapsing is pervasive: 41 percent of firms let at least one patent lapse. Second, alignment varies widely: the lapsed patents’ average value rank is the 59th percentile, with a standard deviation of 24 percentile points across firm-years. Third, formal IP governance is rare: 2.4 percent of firms have an IP committee. Fourth, committee firms’ lapse decisions come closest to the market’s ranking: their lapsed patents average the 51st percentile of value, against the 59th for other firms. Fifth, the association is concentrated in the committee form rather than in an officer title. Within firms, better-aligned years are followed by higher market value and investment. The facts mark patent renewal as a common, widely varying, and largely ungoverned margin of intangible-asset management.
title: IP Governance and Patent Renewal Decisions: Evidence from U.S. Public Firms
title_zh: 知识产权治理与专利续展决策：来自美国上市公司的证据

abstract: Multi-site randomized experiments, which are common in economics and medicine, can reveal how treatment effects vary across settings. However, differences between site-specific estimates reflect both treatment-effect heterogeneity and estimation noise. We build on established measurement-error corrections and develop new ones to study this heterogeneity in experiments with many sites and few units per site. In particular, our results can be used to estimate the variance and centered third moment of treatment effects across sites, relate site effects to untreated outcomes, conduct mediation analyses, assess the roles of provider effectiveness and site responsiveness, and study heterogeneity in local average treatment effects (LATEs) under imperfect compliance. We apply our methods to counseling programs delivered by public and private providers in about 200 French employment offices. Average employment gains of about 2 percentage points conceal cross-site standard deviations of intention-to-treat effects of 8 to 9 percentage points. We also find substantial LATE heterogeneity. Effects are negatively associated with untreated employment rates. The two programs also tend to be more effective in the same sites, consistent with a role for heterogeneous site responsiveness.
title: Estimating treatment-effect heterogeneity across sites, in multi-site randomized experiments with few units per site.
title_zh: 估计多中心随机实验中各中心的处理效应异质性，每中心单位数较少。

abstract: This paper estimates the causal impact of immigration on municipal public finances in Belgium, between 2005 and 2018. Using administrative data on local revenues and expenditures, we study how immigration affects tax collection and public spending (in per capita terms). To address endogeneity, we use an instrumental-variable strategy exploiting historical settlement patterns. While, on average, immigration is associated with lower municipal expenditures and unchanged to slightly lower revenues, these aggregate effects conceal sharp differences: Immigrants from EU countries slighlty increase municipal revenues without significantly affecting expenditures. In contrast, immigration from non-EU countries leads to reductions in: revenues, largely due to a narrower tax base; and in spending, overall and specifically on security and social assistance. The decline in social spending affects non-European immigrants significantly more than Belgian residents, suggesting that municipalities try to shield natives when they face immigration-induced fiscal pressure.
abstract_zh: 本文估计了2005年至2018年间移民对比利时市级公共财政的因果影响。利用地方收入与支出的行政数据，我们研究了移民如何影响税收征收和公共支出（以人均计）。为解决内生性问题，我们采用了一种利用历史定居模式的工具变量策略。虽然平均而言，移民与较低的市级支出以及不变至略低的收入相关，但这些总体效应掩盖了显著差异：来自欧盟国家的移民略微增加了市级收入，而未显著影响支出。相比之下，来自非欧盟国家的移民导致收入减少，这主要归因于税基缩小；以及支出减少，总体支出以及特别是安全和社 会援助方面的支出均有所下降。社会支出的下降对非欧洲移民的影响显著大于对比利时居民的影响，这表明市政当局在面临移民引发的财政压力时试图保护本地居民。
title: Do Immigrants Impact Local Public Finances? Evidence from Belgium
title_zh: 移民是否影响地方公共财政？来自比利时的证据

abstract: As of 2026, humanity is likely below replacement fertility. That has never happened before, not in wars or pandemics. But the real surprise is that the fall has been concentrated in low- and middle-income countries and among poorer and less educated women. We fit a single-factor model to 236 countries since 1950: the common component peaked in 1978, and what drives fertility down today are country-specific trends, 219 of them negative and not one leveling off. None of the commonly cited mechanisms can account for this pattern, so we offer a conjecture: modernity itself, which makes a third child expensive and childlessness cheap. Children come in integers, so it takes very little to move a cohort’s fertility rate from 1.8 to 1.3. And nothing in an economy pushes fertility back to 2.1. We close with the main economic consequences, in particular slow growth.
abstract_zh: 截至2026年，人类很可能已处于更替生育率以下。这在历史上从未发生过，无论战争还是大流行病时期都没有。但真正令人意外的是，生育率下降集中在低收入和中等收入国家，以及较贫困和受教育程度较低的女性群体中。我们对1950年以来236个国家拟合了一个单因子模型：共同成分在1978年达到峰值，而如今推动生育率下降的是各国特有的趋势，其中219个为负向趋势，没有一个趋于平稳。现有常被引用的机制都无法解释这一模式，因此我们提出一个猜想：现代性本身使生育第三个孩子变得昂贵，而使不生育变得廉价。孩子以整数计，因此只需很小的变化就能将一个队列的生育率从1.8推至1.3。而经济中没有任何力量会将生育率推回2.1。我们最后讨论了主要经济后果，尤其是增长放缓。
title: Terra Incognita: The Economics of a Shrinking World
title_zh: 未知领域：一个萎缩世界的经济学

abstract: Propensity to invest in stocks is highly heterogeneous, with many households avoiding stock market participation altogether. This heterogeneity is difficult to reconcile with standard economic theory. We study the role of memories in shaping investment decisions and in influencing how individuals incorporate stock-related information. Across two experiments, participants invest in a stock and are compensated based on its actual price realization. In the first experiment, we verify that activating memories prior to investing systematically shifts investment behavior. Participants asked to recall stock market–related memories before the investment task make more polarized choices: recalling positive memories increases investment relative to recalling non-positive ones, while activating non-positive memories lowers investment compared with not activating them. The second experiment reveals our central finding: the effect of information critically depends on the type of memory activated. All participants recall a memory before investing, after which some receive positive and truthful information about the stock. Information meaningfully increases investment only among participants who recalled non-personal memories; in contrast, recalling personal memories completely eliminates the response to information. We show that this sharp interaction cannot be explained by changes in beliefs, overconfidence, or mistrust in experts. Instead, it can be rationalized within a selective memory framework.
abstract_zh: 投资股票的倾向具有高度异质性，许多家庭完全回避参与股票市场。这种异质性难以与标准经济理论相协调。我们研究记忆在塑造投资决策以及影响个体如何整合股票相关信息方面的作用。通过两项实验，参与者在实验中对一只股票进行投资，并根据其实际价格实现获得报酬。在第一项实验中，我们验证了在投资前激活记忆会系统性地改变投资行为。被要求在投资任务前回忆与股票市场相关记忆的参与者做出了更加两极化的选择：回忆积极记忆相对于回忆非积极记忆会增加投资，而激活非积极记忆相对于不激活则会降低投资。第二项实验揭示了我们的核心发现：信息的作用关键取决于所激活的记忆类型。所有参与者在投资前都会回忆一段记忆，之后部分参与者会收到关于该股票的积极且真实的信息。信息仅在回忆了非个人记忆的参与者中显著增加投资；相比之下，回忆个人记忆完全消除了对信息的反应。我们表明，这种显著的交互作用无法由信念变化、过度自信或对专家的不信任来解释。相反，它可以在选择性记忆框架内得到合理解释。
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
source_issue: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, Volume 250
title: A walk down memory lane: How memories influence stock investment and information processing
title_zh: 追忆往事：记忆如何影响股票投资与信息处理
